standard_prerequisites.name: Higher cohomology of an injective module vanishes

core_obligations: Embed F into an injective I, note that I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for the coverings in Cov, and form the quotient Q = I/F (proof lines 1720-1728).

Use the cofinality assumption and the short exact sequence to obtain a short exact sequence of Cech complexes, because each term of a Cech complex in Cov is a product of values over basis opens, and conclude that Q also has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for coverings in Cov (proof lines 1729-1748).

Run the long exact cohomology sequence over U in B: since H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0 and H^0(U, I) to H^0(U, Q) is surjective, obtain H^1(U, F) = 0; apply the same step to Q to get H^2(U, F) = 0, and continue inductively (proof lines 1751-1775).
proof_roadmap: Resolve F by an injective and transfer the Cech vanishing to the quotient (proof lines 1720-1748).
Read the vanishing of H^p off the long exact sequence and induct on p (proof lines 1751-1775).
difficulty_reason: Let X be a ringed space with a basis B, let F be an O_X-module and let Cov be a set of coverings whose members and finite intersections lie in B, which is cofinal among coverings of each basis open U, and for which all higher Cech cohomology of F vanishes; the lemma concludes H^p(U, F) = 0 for all p > 0 and all U in B (statement lines 1695-1714). The proof embeds F into an injective I, uses that I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for the coverings of Cov, and observes that assumption (1) makes the Cech complex of any U in Cov a product of values over basis opens, so that the short exact sequence 0 to F to I to Q to 0 produces a short exact sequence of Cech complexes and hence Q again has vanishing higher Cech cohomology (proof lines 1720-1748). The proof then runs the long exact cohomology sequence: H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0, surjectivity of H^0(I) to H^0(Q) gives H^1(F) = 0, and the same argument applied to Q gives H^2(F) = 0 and so on by induction (proof lines 1751-1775). The claim is H2: a standard injective-and-induct argument, with the only subtlety being that the cofinality assumption is what makes the basis suffice.
